summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and a history of recurrent pneumonia and COPD, was readmitted one week after discharge due to altered mental status and hypoxia. She was found to have recurrent right lower lobe pneumonia caused by Haemophilus influenzae and MRSA, likely due to aspiration in the setting of opioid use. She had taken methadone without a prescription for chronic pain, contributing to her altered mental status and respiratory compromise. She was treated with vancomycin and meropenem for 10 days, improved clinically, and was weaned off BiPAP. Her sedative medications were reduced by half to minimize respiratory depression. She was discharged home with services, on home oxygen, with follow-up planned for pain management and primary care, and with clear instructions to avoid unprescribed medications.
